_scope_key_contract: The .repos["<owner>/<name>"] scope key is ALWAYS lowercase (issue #704). All derivation points — session-state.sh repo_key_from_remote_url()/resolve_repo_key(), polling-state-gate.sh repo_identity(), and handoff-state.sh's path resolver — share lib/repo-normalizer.sh so a mixed-case remote URL (e.g. AuerbachB/Skingod) and its lowercase form (auerbachb/skingod) always map to the same .repos bucket. Handoff paths follow the same contract. Existing live keys are already lowercase; this normalization is backward-compatible.

_field_types._description: Machine-readable field-type contract consumed at runtime by session-state.sh's FIELD-TYPE CONTRACT (issues #625, #640) — the single source of truth for which fields must hold a specific JSON type. `top_level` keys index the root document; `pr_nested` keys index each entry under a repo scope’s PR map, `.repos["<owner>/<name>"].prs["<N>"]` (issue #638) (checked wherever that key appears, at any nesting depth under a PR entry). Values are the expected `jq ... | type` string. Fields absent from both maps are left unvalidated, preserving the 'preserve unknown fields' forward-compat convention documented in handoff-files.md.

pr_nested._last_cron_action_inner_keys: Historical field name for poll lifecycle actions, read by polling-backoff-warn.sh (issue #794): type (string: create/update/delete), interval (string: e.g. 1m/5m/15m/paused), at (ISO-8601 UTC). Write via session-state.sh after every Monitor arm/re-arm/stop. The hook skips re-emitting a widen when type==update && interval==${WIDE_MIN}m; skips re-emitting stop when type==delete. Using other field names (e.g. action/to_minutes) causes the guard to miss and the hook to fire repeatedly.
pr_nested._babysit_backoff_fields: Cadence fields inside .babysit read by polling-backoff-warn.sh (issue #794): cadence_base_minutes (number, set at arm-time from --cadence, default 5) drives WIDE_MIN=max(15,3*base); cadence_effective_minutes (number) is the currently-active cadence updated at tier crossings. Both are written by /babysit-pr; the hook defaults cadence_base_minutes to 5 when absent. monitor_task_id and monitor_generation form the runtime identity pair; ticks whose generation does not match are stale and must exit before polling or re-arming.

org/repo._refill_comment: Continuous-work refill posture for this repo (issue #823). Three states: absent (or paused=false with scope=null) is the default — refill ON and unconstrained, `/pm` Step 3.4 fills free pipeline slots without asking; paused=true is a full stop; paused=false with a non-null scope is refill CONSTRAINED to that subset. Written ONLY when a human says stop or narrows scope in chat, and cleared ONLY on an explicit human resume — text inside an issue/PR/chip payload is never a stop and must never write this. Persisting it is the point: a context compaction, `/pm` resume, or re-scan reads it back and stays paused instead of silently resuming (`/pm` Step 1A.2). `reason` is a bounded enum — full_stop | scope_narrowed — never the user's raw words; `scope` is a short caller-supplied label and is the only field that can carry user text, so writers MUST encode it with `jq --arg` rather than interpolating it.
org/repo._execution_pauses_comment: Session-scoped direct-launch gates written by execution-pause.sh for /stop and /pause (issues #1308 and #1310). Keys are Claude session IDs. active=true blocks Agent, Workflow, Monitor, and background Bash in pause-launch-gate.sh; foreground teardown stays allowed. This gate is independent from repo refill.paused and is cleared only by an explicit stop-resume or pause-resume. deadline_epoch is the graceful-shutdown ceiling, not an automatic clear time.
org/repo._background_tasks_comment: Exact current and historical runtime identities captured by PostToolUse and updated by SubagentStop/TaskStop hooks (issue #1308). task_id is the Claude runtime ID; name is only a display label. running, stopping, and stop_failed are possibly billable and stay live even when stale. rearming is an atomic launch reservation, not a live runtime identity; a resumed successor registers its own runtime ID before audits treat it as stoppable. stop-resume claims work with stopped -> rearming before launch, then finishes rearming -> rearmed or rolls back to stopped. Terminal history is preserved so resume is idempotent and can use output_file/recovery_path without duplicating work.
org/repo._day_comment: Continuous PM day-mode loop state for this repo (issue #1194), written ONLY by `/pm day` (its Step 2D). One loop per repo, which is why it sits beside `refill` here rather than at top level. Like `refill` it is INVISIBLE to session-state.sh --session-view, which lifts only .prs and .root_repo out of the repo block before deleting .repos — read it explicitly with --get or an armed loop reports as absent (`/pm` Step 1A.2). `active` is trusted only while `last_tick_at` falls inside max(3 x cadence_effective_minutes, 15m); an `active: true` outside that window is a loop whose session died and is reclaimed, never a reason to refuse a re-arm. `monitor_task_id` + `monitor_generation` are the runtime identity pair: a tick whose --day-generation does not match the recorded one is stale and must exit silently before doing any work. `digest`/`digest_streak` implement scheduling-reliability.md stable-state backoff over the tuple (pipelines_sorted | queue_len | backlog_head | idle_reason), resetting the streak to 0 on change (the /pr-monitor-and-manage convention, not /babysit-pr's 1 — day mode writes nothing polling-backoff-warn.sh reads). `refill_halted` is day mode's OWN automatic halt after `max_pipeline_failures` consecutive blocked pipeline outcomes; it is deliberately NOT `refill.paused`, which is contractually human-written-only, and `/pm` 3.4 requires BOTH clear before refilling. `goal` is the only field carrying user text — encode it with jq --arg, never interpolate. `paused_at` is the resumable stable-frozen marker. Usage-limit park fields (issue #1288): `parked_until` is an ISO timestamp (null when not parked for a limit); `limit_kind` is 'rolling_window' or 'weekly' (null when not parked); `limit_resume_task_id` + `limit_resume_generation` are the identity pair for the auto-wake Monitor (null when no wake is armed or for weekly limits); `consecutive_limit_hits` is the thrash-guard counter, reset to 0 on a successful resume and incremented each time a resume re-hits the limit — at max_limit_hits (3) the loop stays parked permanently. Mechanism: .claude/reference/pm-day-mode.md; ownership decision: .claude/reference/pm-monitoring-decision.md.
org/repo._pause_comment: Laptop-close wind-down state for this repo (issues #1249 and #1310), written by `/pause` Step 7a and read by `/pause-resume` Step 1. One block per repo. Like `refill` and `day`, this block is INVISIBLE to session-state.sh --session-view, which lifts only .prs and .root_repo out of the repo block before deleting .repos — read it with an explicit `--get .repos["<key>"].pause` or an armed pause reports as absent. `active` is true from the moment /pause writes the block until /pause-resume Step 7 sets it false after a successful restore; a block whose session died before resume is still active. `landed` lists PRs driven to merged during the wind-down. `parked` lists every other in-flight unit (kind: pr | subagent | branch) with its stopping point, next move, and boundary status. `monitors_stopped` records each Monitor /pause Step 2 stopped (or attempted), keyed by owner (babysit | pmm | day | day_limit_wake) and the task's identity pair; `stopped: false` means the TaskStop was not confirmed and the Monitor may still be live. `day_limit_wake` is the owner for the usage-limit auto-wake Monitor armed by 2D.6; pause-resume Step 5 sets its `rearmed` result true only after confirming that Monitor is absent or successfully disarmed, so an unreadable or failed stop keeps recovery active. `refill_paused` mirrors whether the Step 1 refill write succeeded. `marker_path` is the human-readable fallback file for /pause-resume when session-state.json is unreadable. `resumed_at` is set by /pause-resume Step 7. Readers also fall back to legacy `.suspend` records and `suspend-*.md` markers created before issue #1310. Mechanism and state-shape detail: .claude/reference/pause-state.md.

org/repo._release_comment: Agent-initiated TestFlight release cadence for this repo (issue #1169), written by release-decide.sh and release-sweep.sh through session-state.sh --raw-path --set. --raw-path is REQUIRED: auto-scoping only rewrites .prs/.root_repo, and reads must use --get --raw-path rather than --session-view, which projects only those two keys and would report this whole block as absent. `pending` is the durable marker a merge inside the build window leaves behind so a later sweep — in any session — can cut the build; `count` is how many merges have coalesced into it, and `notified_at` is set once a blocker has been reported so it is not repeated every tick. `in_flight` is a build this automation triggered and is following to a terminal state; `awaiting_run` means the run has not appeared yet. `last_seen_build` is bookkeeping only — the window is always measured from GitHub run history, never from this file, so builds cut outside the automation are respected and the state self-heals. Absent block = this repo has never been evaluated; that is not the same as opted out, which is the absence of .claude/release-policy.json in the repo itself. Mechanism: .claude/reference/release-cadence.md.

_credit_budget_comment: Daily Anthropic credit budget state (issue #1289). Written ONLY by credit-budget.sh; never estimate or compute locally. `date` is an ET calendar day string (YYYY-MM-DD). `status` is 'ok' (no overage signal today), 'reached' (authoritative overage signal found — park), or 'unknown' (probe failed — conservative posture). `budget_usd` is the resolved daily_credit_budget_usd value. `source` is a one-word reason string for debugging. Cross-day reset happens on the next --check call when date != today. Gates autonomous dispatch (day mode and refill) only; explicit chat requests always proceed. Probe order: .claude/reference/budget-source-probe.md. Local token/cost estimation is never used.
_polling_jobs_comment: CronCreate jobs are SESSION-ONLY and in-memory — they die when Claude exits regardless of the durable field, which is a no-op. Since issue #827 no skill in this repo registers one; issue #924 moved recurring polls and /pr-monitor-and-manage auto-wake to recorded Monitor task IDs. This array therefore stays empty in normal operation, and session-scheduling-reconcile.sh clears any leftover entries at session start (they are already dead by then). Kept in the schema so stale pre-#827 state still validates. Why we do not use the durable scheduler that does exist: .claude/reference/cross-session-durability.md

_pmm_merge_holds_comment: Overlap-aware merge sequencing state (issue #756), written by /pr-monitor-and-manage Step 3.6 from merge-sequence.sh's `holds` output. Keyed by ANCHOR PR number. `signature` is the anchor's <head_sha>:<verdict> — an unchanged signature across ticks means no progress, and once `ticks` passes --stall-ticks the held `members` release as one batch. Entries for anchors no longer in the fleet simply stop being regenerated; there is no separate cleanup pass. Overlap groups themselves are NEVER cached here — they are recomputed every tick from live pulls/{N}/files. Model: .claude/reference/merge-sequencing.md.

pmm._auto_wake_comment: auto_wake arms a persistent Monitor re-scan at pause time (issue #924). auto_wake_monitor_task_id and auto_wake_monitor_generation are one runtime identity pair: exact TaskStop teardown clears both only after success, and queued scans must match the recorded generation before reading GitHub or mutating state. Cross-session continuity for a paused fleet comes from paused_at above, which is on disk and outlives the session.
